From 8410186ca48002092818500b7c209e569b47a2ac Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2024 19:53:01 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] arm64/fpsimd: Remove spurious check for SVE support

There is no need to check for SVE support when changing vector lengths,
even if the system is SME only we still need SVE storage for the streaming
SVE state.

Fixes: d4d5be94a878 ("arm64/fpsimd: Ensure SME storage is allocated after SVE VL changes")
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240115-arm64-sve-enabled-check-v1-1-a26360b00f6d@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/kernel/fpsimd.c b/arch/arm64/kernel/fpsimd.c
index 505f389be3e0..0983be2b1b61 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/kernel/fpsimd.c
+++ b/arch/arm64/kernel/fpsimd.c
@@ -898,10 +898,8 @@ int vec_set_vector_length(struct task_struct *task, enum vec_type type,
 	 * allocate SVE now in case it is needed for use in streaming
 	 * mode.
 	 */
-	if (system_supports_sve()) {
-		sve_free(task);
-		sve_alloc(task, true);
-	}
+	sve_free(task);
+	sve_alloc(task, true);
 
 	if (free_sme)
 		sme_free(task);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/arm64/kernel/fpsimd.c`**
- Removed the conditional check for SVE support (`if (system_supports_sve())`) before freeing and allocating SVE storage.
- The calls to `sve_free(task)` and `sve_alloc(task, true)` are now executed unconditionally, regardless of SVE support.

### Relationships
The modification in `fpsimd.c` addresses a bug related to the allocation of SVE storage when changing vector lengths. By removing the spurious check for SVE support, the code ensures that SVE storage is always allocated when needed, even in systems that only support SME (Scalable Matrix Extension). This change is a direct fix to the issue identified in the previous commit (d4d5be94a878), which aimed to ensure proper allocation of SVE storage after changes in vector length.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an unnecessary conditional check for SVE support before freeing and allocating SVE storage. This check led to situations where SVE storage was not allocated when it was needed, particularly in systems that only support SME, resulting in potential issues when changing vector lengths.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (system_supports_sve()) {
    sve_free(task);
    sve_alloc(task, true);
}
```
Reason:
The conditional check for `system_supports_sve()` was unnecessary because even on systems that only support SME, SVE storage is still required for the streaming SVE state. This check could prevent the allocation of SVE storage when it was needed, leading to potential issues when changing vector lengths.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
sve_free(task);
sve_alloc(task, true);
```
Reason:
By removing the conditional check for SVE support, the code now always frees and allocates SVE storage regardless of the system's support for SVE or SME. This ensures that SVE storage is available when changing vector lengths, thus preventing the issues that arose from the previous check.
